feature: NextE-derived Reader immersive chrome and status-bar lifecycle
precondition: An existing complete app-private download was retained. The run records no account state, gallery text, page URL, image content, screenshot, or local file path.
steps: Install the debug-signed HAP with replace semantics, open Downloads, and open the complete task's native Reader.
With the persisted Full screen Reader preference enabled, inspect only safe accessibility indicators: no page counter, no Reader action button, and no status-bar marker.
Tap the canvas once and inspect only safe indicators: page counter 1 / 55, status-bar marker present, and the native back button bounds are [24,135][156,267].
Tap the canvas again and confirm those Reader chrome/status-bar indicators are absent.
Reveal the chrome once more, activate its top back control, and confirm the local Downloads route and its Read control return with the status bar restored.
result: Passed: the Reader uses an overlay chrome that does not reserve canvas height, synchronizes status-bar visibility with the chrome, and restores the prior route before the status bar is returned to the app shell.
cleanup: All temporary device and host accessibility-layout files were removed; the device screen-off timeout was restored to 10000 ms.
